newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Quick sees sales up 10% in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Quick sees sales up 10% in 1997.

text.p: Belgian Quick Restaurants said it expected 1997 sales growth of 10 percent despite difficult economic circumstances and the ongoing beef scare.

"I think we can hope for similar sales growth (in 1997), of about 10 percent, but I would not venture to make a profit forecast," Quick chief executive officer Thomas Meisser told a news conference on Friday.
Total sales rose by 10 percent to 21.5 billion francs in 1996, but this was largely due to the opening of 54 new outlets, bringing the total to 371.

Meisser said the profit plunge in 1996 was due mainly to the scarce over beef linked to mad cow disease, economic gloom, and intense price competition in Belgium with McDonalds, a truckers strike in France in November, where Quick get two-thirds of its turnover, and exceptionally cold weather in December.
"The European crisis over mad cow disease has led to changes in the eating patterns of a number of consumers, who until now still have not regained full confidence in beef," he said.

A poll showed that over 40 percent of French consumers was still concerned about mad cow disease in January, down from 58 percent in June 1996 and 64 percent at the start of the beef crisis in March 1996, he said. Quick would continue to offer more chicken meat based products to counter the beef scare, although beef would remain the core product.
The fast food market kept its growth potential, he said. Quick planned to open about 30 new restaurants this year and would fully renovate 18 existing outlets.
Quick planned to invest 1.7 billion francs in 1997, down from 1.9 billion in 1996.
